item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 291702
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Thu Oct 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located about one hundred miles south-southeast of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure is likely to develop well to the
southeast of the Hawaiian Islands this weekend or early next week.
Thereafter, environmental conditions appear generally favorable for
some slow development of this system as it moves westward to
west-northwestward into the Central Pacific basin.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

item.title: Tropical Depression Vance Public Advisory Number 34
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Thu Oct 29 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 292031
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Vance Advisory Number  34
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 PM MST Thu Oct 29 2026
 
...VANCE WEAKENS WHILE CONTINUING NORTHWARD NEARING THE GULF OF 
CALIFORNIA...
...MOISTURE FROM VANCE WILL SPREAD INTO PORTIONS OF THE
SOUTH-CENTRAL AND SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.3N 108.6W
ABOUT 230 MI...365 KM NW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 95 MI...150 KM ESE OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1008 MB...29.77 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the west-central and northwestern coasts of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Vance
was located near latitude 22.3 North, longitude 108.6 West. The
depression is moving toward the north near 7 mph (11 km/h), this 
motion is expected to continue until Vance dissipates tonight or 
early Friday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 35 mph (55 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Weakening is forecast, and Vance is expected to become 
a post-tropical remnant low this evening.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1008 mb (29.77 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through tonight, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4
inches of rain across central and southern Sinaloa, far southwestern
Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit, with isolated higher totals
over 5 inches possible across central and southern Sinaloa. This
rainfall may produce flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
Moisture carried northeastward from Vance combined with other
Pacific moisture will begin to produce heavy rainfall across the
U.S. Southern Plains and New Mexico today into Friday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect coastal portions of
southwestern and west-central Mexico, as well as the southern
portion of the Baja California Peninsula, during the next day or
so. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Papin

item.title: Tropical Depression Vance Forecast Discussion Number 34
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Thu Oct 29 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 292031
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Depression Vance Discussion Number  34
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 PM MST Thu Oct 29 2026
 
Vance is weakening again. Satellite imagery shows the convective 
structure of Vance has degraded since the previous advisory, as deep 
convection has now shifted about 95 n mi northeast of Vance's 
center. This structure is clear evidence of strong vertical wind 
shear affecting the cyclone. An earlier 1559 UTC Metop-B 
scatterometer pass showed an elongated system with a peak reliable 
wind of 29 kt. The subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB 
was T2.0/30 kt, aligning well with objective aids from UW-CIMSS 
ranging from 28 to 37 kt. Given the recent degradation in satellite 
presentation and the latest intensity estimates, the initial 
intensity is lowered to 30 kt.

The initial motion is estimated to be northward, or 360/6 kt.  This 
general motion at about the same speed is expected until Vance 
degenerates into a trough of low pressure over the southern Gulf of 
California by this evening. The new NHC forecast is largely 
unchanged from the previous one, lying close to the HCCA and TVCN 
aids. The primary hazard associated with Vance remains to be heavy 
rainfall, with high rain rates likely in areas of deep convection 
across north-central Mexico.

Vance continues to feel effects of a hostile environment, 
characterized by strong vertical wind shear of over 50 kt and 
increasingly dry mid-level relative humidity values around 40 to 50 
percent. As a result, the cyclone is soon expected to become a 
remnant low, with most models showing dissipation shortly thereafter 
over the southern Gulf of California. 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact
portions of western Mexico during the next day or two. This rainfall
may produce flooding and mudslides across central and southern
Sinaloa, far southwestern Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
2. Moisture carried northeastward from Vance will produce heavy rain
across portions of the U.S. Southern Plains and New Mexico today
into Friday.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  29/2100Z 22.3N 108.6W   30 KT  35 MPH
 12H  30/0600Z 23.3N 108.7W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 24H  30/1800Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Papin
